ApiToken.description:
An API token of a notebook or a script, by its name, kept only as its SHA-256, which
names it, with when it was made and last used.
ApiToken.title: ApiToken

ApiTokenIdentity.description:
A request of an API token, by the token's name; it needs no CSRF token, since a browser
never sends a bearer token by itself.
ApiTokenIdentity.title: ApiTokenIdentity

ApiTokenRequest.description: The name of a new API token, such as `notebook`.
ApiTokenRequest.title: ApiTokenRequest

AppSettings.description:
The settings the page shows: the server's, from `config.toml`, the data folder, the
theme, and each secret's state.
AppSettings.title: AppSettings

AppliedRunConfig.description:
A run's settings with every default applied (D-51), as its record keeps them: those of
`RunConfig`, each given.
AppliedRunConfig.title: AppliedRunConfig

AtTimeframe.description: A term evaluated on the bars of `timeframe`, each value seen from its bar's close.
AtTimeframe.title: AtTimeframe

BarColumns.description:
A page's bars, column by column, by their open, the bars of one open by their contract:
each bar's open in whole seconds since the Unix epoch, UTC; its trade date; its prices in the
instrument's units, adjusted on a spliced series; its volume, in lots of the dataset's size
unit, a contract, or 0.001 BTC for bitcoin's perpetual; and its contract.
BarColumns.title: BarColumns

BarsPage.description:
A page of a window's bars: the instrument and the timeframe asked for, the provider whose
datasets the bars come from, the bars, the instant the next page opens at, which the caller
sends as the window's start, none on the last page, and what `load` warns of the datasets
the page's bars come from, as a notebook shows it (step 5.4).
BarsPage.title: BarsPage

BinaryOperation.description: An operation on a `left` and a `right` term (module docstring).
BinaryOperation.title: BinaryOperation

Breakdowns.description:
A run's trades by the role of the fill that left them flat (F-TAG-01), the hour of their
entry's fill in the exchange's time zone, the weekday and the year of their entry's trade
date, and the fidelity their entry filled on, each held read-only (`frozen`).
Breakdowns.title: Breakdowns

CatalogProductStatus.description:
A product of the catalog: its root, the first trade date of its history, the name of its
first recommended source, and the datasets of it the store holds, none while it is missing.
CatalogProductStatus.title: CatalogProductStatus

CatalogStatus.description:
The catalog at its version: its products in its order, then the datasets of the roots it
does not list.
CatalogStatus.title: CatalogStatus

CatalogSyncRequest.description:
The product, such as `MES`, whose quality reports a catalog sync writes; every product
the store holds where it is left out.
CatalogSyncRequest.title: CatalogSyncRequest

Column.description:
A column of the signal bars, or of another `instrument`'s bars at the same timeframe,
joined as of each close (`InstrumentInput`).
Column.title: Column

Constant.description: A number or a flag, the same on every bar; a price in the bars' 1e-9 units.
Constant.title: Constant

CoveringDataset.description:
A dataset of a catalog product: complete when it starts by the first trade date of the
product's history, partial when it starts after it.
CoveringDataset.title: CoveringDataset

Currency.description: The currency of an instrument's prices and of what a point is worth.
Currency.title: Currency

DailyStatistics.description:
The statistics of a run's days: a day's profit and loss is the change of the equity at
its trade date's last decision, the first day's from the capital.
DailyStatistics.title: DailyStatistics

DatasetInput.description: A dataset of alternative data by its name, reserved for Phase 10.
DatasetInput.title: DatasetInput

DatasetOrigin.description:
How a dataset came into the store (D-37): imported from the trader's files, or synced
through a connector to a source the trader connects, which waits for a later phase (D-38).
DatasetOrigin.title: DatasetOrigin

DatasetQuality.description:
A dataset's quality: the verdict of its root's report from its provider, as the dataset
reads it, and the last trade date the report checked; the report's findings, those of every
schema of the root, which one verdict covers, the first `FINDINGS_SHOWN` with how many there
are; and the report's coverage by month, none while unchecked (step 5.4).
DatasetQuality.title: DatasetQuality

DayPnl.description: A trade date's profit and loss.
DayPnl.title: DayPnl

DemoJobRequest.description: How many seconds a demo job counts, one a second, from 1 to an hour.
DemoJobRequest.title: DemoJobRequest

DesktopUse.description:
Whether a desktop app on the trader's machine may use the trader's own account or files:
confirmed by the source in writing (none is yet: the confirmations are a Phase 14 kickoff
decision, ADR-0018), to be checked against its terms, or forbidden by them.
DesktopUse.title: DesktopUse

DimensionName.description: A dimension of the robustness summary, in the script's order.
DimensionName.title: DimensionName

DrawdownStatistics.description: The deepest fall of the account below a peak, and its longest spell under one.
DrawdownStatistics.title: DrawdownStatistics

FeatureCode.description: A feature's code: one function under its `@ff.feature(...)` call.
FeatureCode.title: FeatureCode

FeatureInput.description:
Another feature the feature reads, by its name and its content hash; with the
`parameters` it reads it with, where its reader binds them, as a combination does, else those
of the slot given for it, or its defaults; and under the columns of an `alias`, as a slot's,
where its reader names one, else under its outputs' names (step 3.7).
FeatureInput.title: FeatureInput

FeatureOutput.description:
The output `output` of the feature `name` with its `parameters`, the feature found by its
content hash.
FeatureOutput.title: FeatureOutput

FidelityCheck.description:
The error bar of a run's days at lower fidelity (`02` §1.6, step 2.12), `kind` checked:
the period its trade dates finer than a minute span, from `first` to `last`, run from flat
at the run's own fidelity, the baseline, and again at 1-second and at 1-minute fidelity, the
rerun at 1 second none where the period holds no 1-second bars, its dates filling on the
1-minute bars as the rerun at 1 minute does.
FidelityCheck.title: FidelityCheck

FidelityEra.description:
Trade dates in a row on one level, from `first` to `last`, `trade_dates` of them: those a
run filled on, each the finest it held at or coarser than the run's fidelity (`02` §1.6,
D-58), or those whose signal bars `load` built, each from the finest level it holds that
builds the bars (D-71).
FidelityEra.title: FidelityEra

FidelityRerun.description:
The period rerun at a coarser fidelity against the baseline: its outcome; the differences
in trades, net profit and loss, and maximum drawdown, the rerun's less the baseline's; the
fill prices of the trades both entered at one decision on one side; and the trades of the
baseline and of the rerun that the other did not enter.
FidelityRerun.title: FidelityRerun

FieldError.description: Where a request broke the API's schema and why, without the value it sent.
FieldError.title: FieldError

FillPriceDifference.description:
A trade entered at one decision on one side in the baseline and in a rerun: how far the
rerun's entry price and its exits' average price lie from the baseline's, in ticks, the
rerun's less the baseline's.
FillPriceDifference.title: FillPriceDifference

IndexedFeature.description: A saved feature as the index holds it: its row's id, its name, and its versions in order.
IndexedFeature.title: IndexedFeature

IndexedRun.description:
A run as the index holds it: its row's id; when it was asked for, or saved where the index
found it saved; its origin; the strategy version it names, None for one written in a notebook;
its parameters as bound; the trade dates its window spans, its signal bars' once saved; its
settings, every default applied; its status, `succeeded` once its folder is indexed, else its
job's, with the job's progress, message, and error; its job's id, None where the index found
it saved; and its run key once saved, the name of its folder.
IndexedRun.title: IndexedRun

IndexedStrategy.description:
A saved strategy as the index holds it: its row's id, its name, its kind, and its versions
in order.
IndexedStrategy.title: IndexedStrategy

IndexedStrategyVersion.description:
A strategy's version as the index holds it, with the instrument and the timeframe its
strategy names, its hypothesis, and its changelog.
IndexedStrategyVersion.title: IndexedStrategyVersion

IndexedVersion.description:
A saved version as the index holds it: its row's id, its number, its content hash, and when
it was saved.
IndexedVersion.title: IndexedVersion

InstrumentInput.description:
Another instrument's signal bars at the feature's timeframe, such as MNQ's for a feature
of MES, each column suffixed with its root, as `close_MNQ`, with `staleness_MNQ`, the
nanoseconds from that bar's close, joined as of each row's close (step 3.2).
InstrumentInput.title: InstrumentInput

InstrumentKind.description: What trades: a dated futures contract, a perpetual swap, or the asset itself.
InstrumentKind.title: InstrumentKind

InstrumentVersion.description:
A version of an instrument's specification (`fefat.market.instruments`): its root and
kind; its tick size, what a point is worth, and its lot step, in its currency's units; the
name of its session calendar; the trade dates it is in force, from `valid_from` to the day
before `valid_to`; and whether an import saved it, where FEAT does not know the product.
InstrumentVersion.title: InstrumentVersion

IssuedApiToken.description: A new API token under its name, which this response alone carries.
IssuedApiToken.title: IssuedApiToken

Job.description:
A job as the app keeps it (`01-architecture.md` section 6): what it runs and with what,
where it stands, how far it has come, in percent, with its last message, its attempts, the
worker process that holds it and until when its lease runs, when it was asked to stop, and
how it ended.
Job.title: Job

JobKind.description: What a job runs (`01-architecture.md` section 6); a later phase adds its kinds.
JobKind.title: JobKind

JobStatus.description:
Where a job stands (`01-architecture.md` section 6): queued, then running, then one of
four ends, each change a compare-and-set update; a running job whose worker stopped
answering is queued again while it has attempts left (step 4.4, D-90).
JobStatus.title: JobStatus

LimitFill.description:
When a limit fills: once the market trades through its price (F-LMT-01, the default)
or once it touches it (F-LMT-02).
LimitFill.title: LimitFill

LintRule.description:
What a finding of the lint is: a way of reading ahead (`looks_ahead`), a read of data the
detector cannot cut (`fails_validation`), or a warning of what the content hash leaves out.
LintRule.title: LintRule

LoginRequest.description: The password, set at `fefat up`'s first run or by `fefat password set`.
LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest

Metrics.description:
A run's metrics (`02` §7), as `fefat_engine.metrics` works them out, and its fidelity
check, which `fefat.backtest.fidelity_check` adds, told apart by its `kind`.
Metrics.title: Metrics

MonthCoverage.description:
A month of a quality report (`fefat.market.monthly_coverage`): the month, `2026-03`; its
sessions, those with records of any schema, those with ticks, with 1-second bars, and with
1-minute bars; its findings; and the sessions touching a UTC day the vendor flagged.
MonthCoverage.title: MonthCoverage

NewFeature.description:
A new feature: its name, the name of the function its code defines, and its first
version's code.
NewFeature.title: NewFeature

NewStrategy.description:
A new strategy: its name, a lower-case identifier of at most 64 characters, and its first
version.
NewStrategy.title: NewStrategy

NewStrategyVersionRequest.description:
A version to save: its code, its hypothesis, one sentence on one line stating the edge,
and its changelog.
NewStrategyVersionRequest.title: NewStrategyVersionRequest

OrderRole.description:
What an order does for a position, which its fill records (F-TAG-01): open it, protect it
(an exit plan's stop), take its profit (target 1 to 3), close it at the market, for the
strategy's own reason (`exit`) or an execution template's exit reason (§20), or carry it
across a roll, a leg of the roll for its reason (F-ROL-02).
OrderRole.title: OrderRole

Outcome.description: A group of trades: how many, how many won, and their profit and loss.
Outcome.title: Outcome

OutputKind.description:
What an output's values are (D-71), which its column must admit and its version keeps; the
leak detector compares values by their column's type. A `price` (a level, such as a moving
average) and a `price_distance` (such as an ATR) are in the bars' 1e-9 units, the units in
which the execution template reads them (F-RND-01, D-60), never in points.
OutputKind.title: OutputKind

PasswordChange.description: The password the session's login used, and the one to keep in its place.
PasswordChange.title: PasswordChange

PeriodOutcome.description:
The fidelity check's period run from flat at one fidelity: the eras its trade dates filled
on, its trades, their net profit and loss, and its maximum drawdown, the capital first.
PeriodOutcome.title: PeriodOutcome

PinnedFeature.description:
A feature version a strategy's slots read, as the library keeps it: its name, its number,
and its content hash.
PinnedFeature.title: PinnedFeature

Preset.description: A file layout FEFAT imports; its id is the provider its datasets are stored under.
Preset.title: Preset

PresetStatus.description:
Whether FEFAT reads a preset's files yet: the Databento importer of step 1.6 does, and
the presets of step 1.10 are planned.
PresetStatus.title: PresetStatus

Problem.description: An error the API answered (RFC 9457), with the id of the request it ended.
Problem.title: Problem

QualityFinding.description:
What a report finds wrong with a dataset on a trade date: a session without records,
repeated records, records outside their session and its break, decreases of the clock
between stored rows, prices of zero or below where none are allowed, and bars that differ
from those rebuilt from finer data.
QualityFinding.title: QualityFinding

QualityStatus.description:
A root's verdict from one provider: no finding, some, no report yet, or a clean report a
dataset outgrew, whose last trade date checked is before the dataset's last (step 1.9) or
that is older than a partition of the dataset (step 5.1).
QualityStatus.title: QualityStatus

RedFlag.description: A red flag that fires, with the script's message.
RedFlag.title: RedFlag

RedFlagId.description: A red flag of the script's checklist.
RedFlagId.title: RedFlagId

RefusedCheck.description:
A fidelity check, `kind` refused, whose rerun at `fidelity` the engine refused, with its
message, as when a trade date of the period holds no level at or coarser than it, ticks
without bars.
RefusedCheck.title: RefusedCheck

RefusedCode.description:
Code the SDK refused: the line of the code the refusal is at, None where it has none, and
why, in the SDK's words.
RefusedCode.title: RefusedCode

RefusedCodeProblem.description:
The trader's code the SDK refused (step 5.2), with the line of the code the refusal is
at, None where it has none, which an editor underlines.
RefusedCodeProblem.title: RefusedCodeProblem

Replay.description:
How the Rust engine replays a run: every record in turn, or skipping the blocks of
records that no order can act on, by the coarser bars above them (`02` §4). Both give the
same fills, so a run's key leaves it out.
Replay.title: Replay

ReportedFinding.description:
A finding of a quality report: its trade date, its kind, the schema and the contract it
was found in, none for a gap, which no contract fills, and how many records or bars it
counts.
ReportedFinding.title: ReportedFinding

Robustness.description:
The robustness summary of a run: what the script read, its five scores, their total and
verdict, its red flags, the sample size the run reaches, the script's profit factor (none
where the script's is infinite) and expectancy in percent of the capital per trade, and the
profit and loss at one more tick of slippage, `fragile_to_slippage` when the run's profit is
gone at it. The regimes a run covers arrive with step 11.4 (D-51).
Robustness.title: Robustness

RollHandling.description:
What a roll does with an open position: transfer it to the new front (F-ROL-02, the
default), or close it (F-ROL-04).
RollHandling.title: RollHandling

RunConfig.description:
A backtest's settings: `fidelity`, the finest data it fills on, each trade date on its
finest level at or coarser than it (D-58), the finest the store holds when left out;
`latency_ms` from a decision to its orders' activation (F-ACT-01); `slippage_ticks` of market
and stop orders, by default none on TBBO and one on every other fidelity, the run's fidelity
setting deciding, whatever level a date falls back to (F-SLP-01); `limit_fill`
(F-LMT-01, F-LMT-02); `roll_handling` (F-ROL-02, F-ROL-04); `fee_table`, a table of
`fefat.market.fees`, by default `retail-default` for futures and `binance-default` for crypto;
`capital`, in the instrument's currency; `replay`, skipping what no order can act on or in
full, which give the same fills (`02` §4); `provider`, as `load` takes it; and `contract`,
one contract of the strategy's root read unspliced, as `load` reads a contract, so that the
run crosses no roll and needs no roll calendar (step 2.14, D-59), by default the roll
calendar's fronts.
RunConfig.title: RunConfig

RunOrigin.description:
Where a run's row comes from: asked for through the API, or found saved by the index; the
batches of later phases add theirs.
RunOrigin.title: RunOrigin

RunStrategy.description:
The saved strategy version a run names, as the index holds it: the strategy's row's id and
name, and the version's row's id and number.
RunStrategy.title: RunStrategy

RunSubmission.description:
A backtest of a saved strategy version: the id of the version's row, which
`GET /v1/strategies` gives; its parameters, its defaults filling those left out; the trade
dates from `start` to `end`; and its settings, each left out taking its default, which the
run's answer gives with every default applied.
RunSubmission.title: RunSubmission

RunWithMetrics.description:
A run with what its record says of how it went, once saved: its metrics, the fidelity era
of each trade date it filled on, and its warnings; none of them before.
RunWithMetrics.title: RunWithMetrics

SampleSize.description:
Which of the skill's trade counts a run reaches: an absolute minimum of 30, 100
preferred, and 200 for high confidence.
SampleSize.title: SampleSize

SavedFeatureVersion.description:
A feature version as the API gives it: its file's record (`fefat.features.versions`), and
its row's id and its feature's in the index.
SavedFeatureVersion.title: SavedFeatureVersion

SavedStrategyVersion.description:
A strategy version as the API gives it: its file's record (`fefat.strategy.versions`),
its row's id and its strategy's in the index, and the lint's findings in its code, which
warn.
SavedStrategyVersion.title: SavedStrategyVersion

ScriptInputs.description:
What the skill's script reads of a run, under its own names: the trades, the win rate in
percent, the average win, the average loss over the trades that did not win (the script takes
every trade that is not a win as a loss, so it differs from `TradeStatistics.average_loss`
when a trade breaks even), and the maximum drawdown, in percent of the capital, the years the
window spans rounded to the nearest, the parameters (the numbers the execution template sets
apart from their defaults), and whether the run paid slippage or fees.
ScriptInputs.title: ScriptInputs

SecretName.description:
The secrets FEAT keeps, each the key of a service it calls: the agent's model provider
(Phase 8) and a market data vendor (D-37). The list is closed, since a credential store
cannot list what it holds; a step that calls another service adds its name.
SecretName.title: SecretName

SecretState.description: Whether the credential store holds a secret.
SecretState.title: SecretState

SecretStatus.description: A secret by its name, with whether it is stored, never with its value.
SecretStatus.title: SecretStatus

SessionIdentity.description:
A request of a login session, with the CSRF token that every state-changing request the
session's cookie authenticates must carry in `X-CSRF-Token`, and when the session ends.
SessionIdentity.title: SessionIdentity

Settings.description:
What the server needs before its database opens, from `<FEFAT_HOME>/config.toml`
(`01-architecture.md` sections 4, 6, and 8, D-83): the port it listens on, the address it
binds, which can only be the loopback (D-54), the size of its process pool, and the folders
an import may read large files from. What the app edits, such as the password and the
theme, lives in its database's `settings` table instead; secrets live in the credential
store, never here.
Settings.title: Settings

SettingsChange.description:
A change of the settings: a secret named with a value stores it, one named with null
removes it, and one left out stays as it is; a theme, when given, replaces the theme.
SettingsChange.title: SettingsChange

Severity.description: How serious a red flag is.
Severity.title: Severity

SlippageTicks.description: Ticks by which market and stop-market fills are worse than their reference (F-SLP-01).
SlippageTicks.title: SlippageTicks

Source.description:
A source of market data as the guide describes it; `terms_page` is null where the source
publishes no terms page, and `licence_scope` is copied into every dataset imported from it.
Source.title: Source

SourceGuide.description: Every known source in the order the guide prints them, as read on `researched_on`.
SourceGuide.title: SourceGuide

SourceKind.description:
What a source is: a data vendor, an exchange's own archive, or a trading platform whose
exports a preset reads.
SourceKind.title: SourceKind

StoredDataset.description:
A dataset of trades, TBBO, or bars the store holds (`fefat.market.status`): its id; its
provider, root, schema, and fidelity, `trades`, `tbbo`, or the timeframe of its bars; how
many contracts it holds and its first and last trade date; the quality of its root's report
from its provider, with the last trade date the report checked, none while unchecked; its
origin and the licence scope of its source; and the last day a file of its provider that fed
its root was imported, none without a record of one.
StoredDataset.title: StoredDataset

StrategyCode.description: A strategy's code, a module whose function `strategy` gives the `SignalStrategy`.
StrategyCode.title: StrategyCode

StrategyKind.description:
What a strategy is: a signal strategy (`SignalStrategy`), the only kind until the event
strategies of Phase 9.
StrategyKind.title: StrategyKind

StrategyLintFinding.description:
A finding of a strategy's lint: its rule, the line of the code it is on, the line's text,
and why it reads ahead or reads data.
StrategyLintFinding.title: StrategyLintFinding

StrategyTemplate.description:
A strategy to start from: its name, its hypothesis, one sentence stating the edge, and its
code, a strategy version's (`fefat.strategy.source_code`).
StrategyTemplate.title: StrategyTemplate

Theme.description:
The web app's colours (`web/DESIGN.md`): dark, the default the design brief sets, or
light.
Theme.title: Theme

TickFidelity.description: Tick data: trades with the quote just before each, or trades alone.
TickFidelity.title: TickFidelity

TimeUnit.description: The unit of a bar timeframe, as the schema name writes it.
TimeUnit.title: TimeUnit

Timeframe.description: A bar's length, written `1s`, `5m`, `1h`, or `1d`; a daily bar spans its trade date.
Timeframe.title: Timeframe

TimeframeInput.description:
The timeframe of the bars the feature is evaluated on, such as `15m` for a feature that a
strategy of 5-minute bars reads, which sees each value from its bar's close (step 3.2).
TimeframeInput.title: TimeframeInput

TradeStatistics.description: The statistics of a run's trades, money in the instrument's currency.
TradeStatistics.title: TradeStatistics

TradesInput.description:
The instrument's prints of each bucket of the feature's bars by aggressor side, available
at the bucket's close, as `buy_volume`, `sell_volume`, and `unknown_side_volume`, null where
no prints are in hand (step 3.6, `fefat.market.aggressor`), as cumulative delta reads them.
TradesInput.title: TradesInput

ValidStrategy.description:
A strategy's code that builds: the instrument and the timeframe its strategy names with
its defaults, the JSON schema of its parameters, and the lint's findings in its code, which
warn (`ff.strategy.lint`).
ValidStrategy.title: ValidStrategy

ValidationProblem.description: A request the API's schema refused, with each of its errors.
ValidationProblem.title: ValidationProblem

Verdict.description: The plain verdict of the total: 70 points or more, 40 or more, or fewer.
Verdict.title: Verdict

VersionDiff.description:
The unified diff of the code of two versions, `earlier`'s and `later`'s, empty where their
code is the same; the structured diff of a builder's spec joins it with the builder of
Phase 6.
VersionDiff.title: VersionDiff

Versions.description:
The versions the server runs: the app's, the SDK's, and the engine's three, which every
run records (`02-engine-and-data.md` section 4).
Versions.title: Versions

Weekday.description: A day of the week, as the specification spells it.
Weekday.title: Weekday

Window.description: A window over the last `n` bars of a term, `lag` the term `n` bars before.
Window.title: Window

ApiToken.description: An API token of `fefat token create`, for notebooks and scripts.

CsrfToken.description: The `csrf_token` of `POST /v1/auth/login` or `GET /v1/me`, which every request that changes state must carry when the session's cookie authenticates it.
CsrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token

Session.description: The login session's cookie, which `POST /v1/auth/login` sets.
Session.name: fefat_session

info.description: FEAT's local server: its API, for the web app, notebooks, and scripts.
info.title: FEAT

get.description:
The API tokens not revoked, by when they were made, with when each was last used, never
a token.

schema.title: Response Live Api Tokens V1 Api Tokens Get

post.description:
Make an API token, shown in this response alone; refused with 409 for a name a live
token has, while a revoked token's name is free.

delete.description:
Revoke the live API token `name`, which every request refuses from then on; refused with
404 where no live token has the name.

post.description:
Log in with the password: the response sets the cookie of a session of 30 days and
returns its CSRF token; refused with 401 for a wrong password, and with 429 after five
attempts in a minute.

End the session the cookie names, whether the cookie or an API token authenticates the
request, and clear the cookie.

Change the password, from a login session alone: every session ends, every API token is
revoked, and the response sets the cookie of a new one for this browser and returns its CSRF
token; refused with 403 for a wrong current password, and with 429 after five attempts in a
minute, the logins' attempts included.

get.description:
The products of the catalog, each with its history's first trade date, its first
recommended source, and the datasets that cover it, complete or partial, none where it is
missing; then the datasets of the roots the catalog does not list.

post.description:
Start the catalog sync of `root`, or of every product: a job that writes the quality
report of each provider's data of it, as `fefat data quality` does, queued until a worker of
the pool is free; refused with 404 where the store holds no trades or bars of it.

get.description:
Every dataset of trades, TBBO, or bars the store holds, by provider, root, and schema,
with its trade dates, fidelity, and quality.

schema.title: Response Stored Datasets V1 Datasets Get

get.description:
The quality of the dataset `dataset_id` names, `provider:schema:root` such as
`databento:ohlcv-1m:MES`, with the findings of its root's report; refused with 404 where the
store holds no such dataset.
The saved features by name, each with its versions in order.

schema.title: Response Saved Features V1 Features Get

post.description:
Create the feature `name` with its first version, saved in the executor; refused with 400
and the line of the code where it defines no feature, or another, and with 409 where a saved
feature has the name or the library holds files the index cannot follow.

get.description: The unified diff of the code of versions `from` and `to` of the feature.

Cancel the job `job_id`: at once while it is queued; while it runs, it is asked to stop,
which its worker does at its next report, or which the server makes it do ten seconds
later; an ended job is given as it is. Refused with 404 where no job has the id.

as `ff.market.load` gives them, column by column; `next_from` is the instant the next page
opens at, to send as `from`, none on the last page. Refused with 404 for an instrument that
names no root and no contract of one, and with 400, in the SDK's words, for a window it
refuses, such as one a provider named does not hold.

holds files the index cannot follow.
